entries.decision: Sparkline bar colors are always computed via continuous blend_colors() interpolation between min_color and max_color — never via discrete threshold buckets.
entries.reasoning: Discrete buckets produced visually jarring hard edges when adjacent bars had close values; continuous blending reads as a smooth gradient and matches the rest of the widget library's color-blend conventions.
rejected_alternatives: Fixed N-color threshold buckets (e.g. red/yellow/green bands)

entries.decision: New Sparkline visual features (markers, overlays, alternate bar treatments) belong in the renderables/sparkline.py rendering logic, not in the widgets/_sparkline.py widget wrapper.
entries.reasoning: The renderable is reused by anything that wants a sparkline-shaped Rich renderable without the full Widget/CSS machinery; keeping visual logic there keeps that reuse path intact. The widget wrapper should stay a thin CSS/component-class adapter over it.
rejected_alternatives: Implementing new visual features directly in the widget wrapper for faster access to component-class styling

entries.decision: All widget snapshot tests live as functions inside the single tests/snapshot_tests/test_snapshots.py file, keyed to a snapshot app or example under snapshot_apps/ or docs/examples/widgets/ — there are no per-widget test_<widget>.py files under tests/snapshot_tests/.
entries.reasoning: A single file keeps the snap_compare fixture wiring and the __snapshots__ directory mapping in one place, and matches how syrupy's snapshot naming already keys off the test function name rather than the file name.
rejected_alternatives: One test_<widget>.py file per widget under tests/snapshot_tests/, mirroring the tests/renderables/ layout
